source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_name: Acacia angustissima (Mill.) Kuntze var. hirta (Nutt.) B.L. Rob.
taxonomic_crosswalk_note: Acacia angustissima var. hirta synonym of Acaciella angustissima var. texensis confirmed by Kew POWO

morphology_source_reported.habit: Unarmed herbaceous perennial or low subshrub, ca. 1 m or less [genus key]
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Bipinnate; 6–16 pairs of pinnae, sensitive leaflets that fold on touch, rain or at night
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Cream-white staminal filaments; solitary or few axillary and terminal globose heads in erect leafy racemes
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Flat, 5–7 cm long and 6–10 mm broad [key]

habitat_source_reported: Prairies on calcareous clay; also sand
cautions: Do not infer Hays County nativity from Flora regional statements
